kb/Work PB354. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 6 and 6) b) 1.): for indexed files data-name-1 shall reference either a) a prime or alternate record key associated with file-name-1, or b) a data item whose 'leftmost character position WITHIN A RECORD OF THE FILE corresponds to the leftmost character position of a prime or alternate record key that is associated with file-name-1 and that is defined without the SOURCE phrase in the RECORD KEY clause or ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause'.
LANDED 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB354). SR6's two arms are two methods. a) RecordLayout.KeyIndexOfKeyItem: the operand IS a record key - by reference identity, or by 12.4.5.12.4 GR4's identical BYTE POSITIONS in another record description entry OF THE SAME FILE. b) RecordLayout.GenericKeyIndex: SR6 b)'s three conditions together. The missing premise of b) 1. - "within a record of the file" - is required by RecordLayout.IsInRecordOfFile, so a WORKING-STORAGE 01 at offset 0 no longer collides with offset 0 in the record (conformance:cases/14.9.41-START/pb354-start-operand-outside-record). The COMPLEMENT is measured, not assumed: conformance:cases/12.4.5.12-RECORD-KEY/pb354_start_generic_key_ok walks all five accepting shapes (declared prime key, a GR4 implicit key in a second record description, a shorter generic prime key, the declared alternate, and a shorter generic alternate) and each returns the record the rule selects.
CODE-LOCATION RENAME 2026-09-06 (kb/Work PB699), verdict and reasoning unchanged: the private RecordLayout.InRecordOfFile became the PUBLIC nullable-tolerant IsInRecordOfFile, because it is the same predicate three file control entry rules are stated on - 12.4.5.12.3 SR2 and 12.4.5.6.3 SR2 REQUIRE a record key to be within a record of the file, 12.4.5.13.3 SR3 FORBIDS it of the relative key - and a second copy in FileControlKeyRules would have been one rule written down twice. The rename is recorded as a BATCH rather than a hand edit so the lander can re-apply it on the merged tree.
